chunks.title: Why Clarteon exists
chunks.text: Most technology projects start with a tool looking for a problem. Clarteon starts the other way around. We find the repetitive work or the broken handoff that is slowing a business down, then recommend the clearest way to fix it. Sometimes that is automation. Sometimes it is a chatbot, a piece of custom software, a website, or a connection between tools you already use.

chunks.title: What to expect on a discovery call
headingPath: What to expect on a discovery call
chunks.text: A short conversation about the problem, not a sales presentation. We ask what is slowing you down, what you have tried, and what a good outcome looks like. We look for the smallest useful next step, not the biggest possible project. You leave with a clear idea of the likely direction and whether we are a fit. If we are not the right fit, we say so and point you toward a better option. No preparation is required beyond a rough description of the problem.

chunks.title: Clara, our AI assistant
chunks.text: Clara is an AI assistant. When you chat with her, the messages you send are processed by our AI provider, Groq, so she can reply. Groq receives the conversation text needed to generate a reply. Groq's privacy policy states that it does not retain inputs and outputs by default, and that it may keep them for up to 30 days for reliability and abuse monitoring. We do not store your chat transcript in our lead database. Cloudflare Turnstile checks that you are a person before your first message. If Clara cannot answer from our published content, we log the question with names, email addresses and other personal details removed, so a person can review it and improve our answers. We keep those notes only as long as needed for that purpose. Please do not share passwords, payment details, government identification or other sensitive information in chat. If you are under 18, please do not use the chat or share personal details.

chunks.title: Discovery-call bookings
chunks.text: When you book a discovery call, we collect your name, email address, the time you choose, your timezone and any notes you add. We use Neon to store the booking record, Resend to send confirmation emails, and Google Calendar to create the event and its Google Meet link. Google processes the event details and sends the calendar invitation. We keep booking details only as long as needed to arrange and follow up on the call, then delete them unless a client relationship or law requires a longer period. You can ask us to remove your booking details sooner.

chunks.title: How long we keep project briefs
headingPath: How long we keep project briefs
chunks.text: We keep project briefs for 12 months from submission, then delete or anonymize them, unless a conversation is active and needs the history. You can ask us to remove your brief sooner.

chunks.title: Site analytics
chunks.text: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics to count page visits and measure how fast pages load. It does not set cookies, and Cloudflare states that it does not track individual visitors across other websites. When a page loads, your browser sends Cloudflare information about that visit, such as the page address and how long it took to load. We see only totals, not individual visitors.

chunks.title: What the project brief form collects
headingPath: What the project brief form collects
chunks.text: When you send a project brief, we collect your name, email address, optional company and team size, and the message you write. We also receive the time of submission and the technical signal from our bot check. We use this information only to reply to you and to keep the form safe. The form saves your brief in our lead database before sending any email. Our providers are Neon (database hosting), Resend (email delivery), Cloudflare Turnstile (bot check) and Vercel (hosting). Each provider processes the data needed for its part of the service.
